stories.headline: The desk has arrived, and five people are already yelling
stories.body:
Imaginary Football now has a newsroom, which is unfortunate for everyone involved.

The standings, waiver bids, trades and lineup decisions still come straight from Sleeper. Those numbers are the facts. What they mean is where the five analysts intend to make your Sunday substantially louder.

Nobody on this desk is obligated to agree with anybody else. In fact, agreement is viewed as a clerical error.

takes.text: I've played this game at the highest level. You look at a matchup like this and you don't just see points. You see momentum, confidence, and somebody finding out what fourth-quarter football feels like.

I have reviewed the league. I have reviewed the rosters. And I am telling you right now: somebody in this league is walking around with far too much confidence. I will not name names yet. But they know.

Before anyone tells me who 'looks good,' show me the usage. Opportunity, efficiency, expected points, and lineup decisions are measurable. Vibes are not a statistic, despite how aggressively this desk uses them.

I have seen enough. Some of you are managing fantasy football like it is a group project, and I am here to identify the person who did not do the reading. Your roster is not 'building.' It is simply confused.
LET'S GOOOO! Five analysts! Twelve teams! Waivers! Trades! DRAMA! Somebody make a move that makes absolutely no sense and then call me immediately because I need to talk about it for twenty minutes!

stories.storyline: Which manager is actually controlling the league, and which manager has simply benefited from a few numbers breaking their way?
